t: Funds appropriated by this title shall not be available for obligation unless the Secretary of State or the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, as appropriate, has notified the Committees on Appropriations in writing at least 15 days in advance of such obligation: Provided, That the requirement of this section shall not apply to funds made available by this title under the headings “Department of State—Administration of Foreign Affairs—Office of Inspector General”, “United States Agency for International Development—Funds Appropriated to the President—Office of Inspector General”, “Bilateral Economic Assistance—Funds Appropriated to the President—International Disaster Assistance”, and “Bilateral Economic Assistance—Department of State—Migration and Refugee Assistance”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a mandatory advance notification before funds may be obligated is a form of consultation before a federal decision. But the only recipients are the congressional Committees on Appropriations, which are inside the federal government, and the notifying parties are federal officials. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is involved, and no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: has notified the Committees on Appropriations in writing at least 15 days in advance of such obligation

opus.w: The only procedural requirement is that the Secretary of State or the USAID Administrator notify the congressional Committees on Appropriations before obligating funds. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so this is a notification within the government, not outside participation. The advance-notice language looks procedural, but no party outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in the decision.
opus.s: has notified the Committees on Appropriations in writing at least 15 days in advance of such obligation
opus.b: The tempting reading is that a formal 15-day advance written notice before funds are obligated is a procedural step that brings someone else into the decision. That reading doesn't hold up. The notice goes to the Committees on Appropriations, which are part of Congress and therefore inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of State or USAID Administrator to notify the Committees on Appropriations (Congress) before obligating funds. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Notification to Congress is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: Funds appropriated by this title shall not be available for obligation unless the Secretary of State or the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, as appropriate, has notified the Committees on Appropriations in writing at least 15 days in advance of such obligation
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying Congress is a form of participation because it involves an external check on executive power. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, notification to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
